title: COVID-19 (adult): severity-based treatment
subject: infectious-disease
summary: Grade severity by SpO2 and respiratory rate. Non-severe but high risk: nirmatrelvir-ritonavir within 5 days. Severe or critical: oxygen, dexamethasone 6 mg for up to 10 days, an IL-6 receptor blocker or baricitinib, and prophylactic-dose anticoagulation. No steroids or empirical antibiotics for non-severe disease.

sections.title: Grade severity
items: Critical (WHO): ARDS, sepsis or septic shock, or need for life-sustaining treatment (invasive or non-invasive ventilation, vasopressors).
Severe (WHO): any of SpO2 below 90% on room air, respiratory rate above 30/min, or signs of severe respiratory distress (accessory muscle use, unable to complete sentences).
Non-severe: none of the criteria for severe or critical disease.

ICMR/AIIMS clinical guidance (India): mild, upper respiratory symptoms without breathlessness or hypoxia; moderate, respiratory rate 24/min or more or SpO2 90 to 93% on room air; severe, respiratory rate above 30/min or SpO2 below 90% on room air.

Higher risk of progression: older age, immunocompromise (transplant, chemotherapy, uncontrolled HIV), chronic lung, heart, kidney or liver disease, diabetes, obesity, and no or incomplete vaccination.

sections.title: Investigations
items: Confirm with a rapid antigen test or RT-PCR; use RT-PCR if the antigen test is negative but suspicion is high.
Severe or admitted: CBC, CRP, creatinine, liver function, glucose, D-dimer, chest X-ray (or CT or lung ultrasound), and a blood gas if hypoxic.
Blood cultures and procalcitonin only when bacterial co-infection is suspected. Check HBsAg before tocilizumab or baricitinib.

sections.title: Non-severe
items: Symptomatic care (paracetamol, fluids), isolation and pulse oximetry; return if breathless or SpO2 is 93% or below.

High risk of hospitalisation, within 5 days of symptoms: nirmatrelvir 300 mg plus ritonavir 100 mg orally every 12 hours for 5 days (eGFR 30 to 59: 150/100 mg every 12 hours). Check every drug interaction first.
If nirmatrelvir-ritonavir cannot be used: remdesivir 200 mg IV on day 1, then 100 mg IV on days 2 and 3, started within 7 days of symptom onset (WHO conditional; IDSA).
Do not give corticosteroids, empirical antibiotics, ivermectin, hydroxychloroquine, colchicine or convalescent plasma for non-severe COVID-19.

sections.title: Severe and critical
items: Oxygen to SpO2 92 to 96% (88 to 92% if at risk of hypercapnia); WHO accepts above 90% once stable and 92 to 95% in pregnancy. Step up through nasal prongs, face mask, high-flow nasal oxygen or non-invasive ventilation, and use awake prone positioning where tolerated.
Dexamethasone 6 mg IV or orally once daily for up to 10 days; alternatives are prednisolone 40 mg daily or hydrocortisone 50 mg IV every 8 hours.

Add an IL-6 receptor blocker, tocilizumab 8 mg/kg IV once (actual body weight, maximum 800 mg), or baricitinib 4 mg orally once daily for 14 days or until discharge (WHO strong recommendation for both). Use one of them; evidence for combining them is limited.
Severe disease on low-flow oxygen: remdesivir 200 mg IV on day 1, then 100 mg daily for 4 days may be considered (WHO conditional); not for critical disease.

Standard prophylactic-dose anticoagulation for all admitted severe or critical patients (for example enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily) unless contraindicated; therapeutic dose only for confirmed VTE or another indication.

Critical: lung-protective ventilation (tidal volume 4 to 8 mL/kg predicted body weight, plateau pressure below 30 cmH2O), prone ventilation for 12 to 16 hours a day in moderate to severe ARDS, and conservative fluids.
Give antibiotics only when bacterial infection is suspected (WHO 2025 advises against empirical antibiotics when suspicion is low).

sections.title: Monitoring
items: SpO2 and respiratory rate at least 4-hourly; watch for silent hypoxaemia.
Capillary glucose on dexamethasone; target 140 to 180 mg/dL (7.8 to 10 mmol/L) in hospital.
Tocilizumab and baricitinib raise infection risk: watch for bacterial and fungal infection, and consider latent TB and strongyloidiasis in endemic settings.

COVID-associated mucormycosis (seen widely in India in 2021): avoid unnecessary or high-dose steroids, control glucose, and act on facial pain, nasal discharge, periorbital swelling or palatal eschar.

sections.title: Special groups and interactions
items: Pregnancy: use prednisolone 40 mg orally daily or hydrocortisone 80 mg IV twice daily instead of dexamethasone (unless steroids are being given for fetal lung maturity); target SpO2 92 to 95%; involve obstetrics.

Nirmatrelvir-ritonavir interactions: hold or adjust statins, many anticoagulants and antiarrhythmics, calcineurin inhibitors and some antiepileptics; rifampicin, carbamazepine and phenytoin rule it out.
Renal: baricitinib 2 mg daily for eGFR 30 to 59, 1 mg daily for 15 to 29, and avoid below 15; nirmatrelvir-ritonavir dose is halved for eGFR 30 to 59.
Immunocompromised patients can shed virus and relapse for longer; seek specialist advice on prolonged or repeated antiviral courses.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Dexamethasone for non-severe patients without hypoxia, or high-dose steroid pulses.
Routine antibiotics or antifungals without evidence of bacterial or fungal infection.
Starting nirmatrelvir-ritonavir without an interaction check.
Therapeutic anticoagulation for all admitted patients without a specific indication.

drugs.name: Nirmatrelvir-ritonavir
drugs.dose: 300 mg/100 mg orally every 12 hours for 5 days; eGFR 30 to 59: 150 mg/100 mg every 12 hours
drugs.notes: Non-severe, high risk, within 5 days of symptoms. Check interactions.

drugs.name: Remdesivir
drugs.dose: 200 mg IV on day 1, then 100 mg IV daily on days 2 to 3 (non-severe, high risk) or days 2 to 5 (severe)

drugs.name: Dexamethasone
drugs.dose: 6 mg IV or orally once daily for up to 10 days
drugs.notes: Severe or critical only. Monitor glucose.

drugs.name: Tocilizumab
drugs.notes: Severe or critical, with corticosteroids. Check HBsAg; infection risk.

drugs.name: Baricitinib
drugs.dose: 4 mg orally once daily for 14 days or until discharge; eGFR 30 to 59: 2 mg; 15 to 29: 1 mg
drugs.notes: Alternative to an IL-6 receptor blocker. Avoid below eGFR 15.

drugs.name: Enoxaparin
drugs.dose: 40 mg SC once daily (30 mg once daily if creatinine clearance below 30 mL/min)
drugs.notes: Thromboprophylaxis for admitted severe or critical patients.
